item.text: {"status":"confirmed","reasoning":"Differentiating y=C/x² and substituting C=x²y gives the original slope −2y/x. Its negative reciprocal is x/(2y). Integrating 2y dy=x dx yields y²=x²/2+A, equivalently 2y²−x²=K with K=2A. This agrees with Math Academy's stated answer, 2y²−x²=K; its reuse of K amounts to renaming the arbitrary constant.
